gaps.sentence: Nobody volunteered to stay late, ___ Tomas.
gaps.explanation: 'Apart from Tomas' = except for Tomas, the only person who volunteered.

gaps.sentence: My sister is terribly reserved, ___ I'll talk to complete strangers.
gaps.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts two parallel facts: her nature versus mine.

gaps.sentence: He was warned repeatedly; ___, he ignored every safety rule.
gaps.explanation: He ignored the warnings despite receiving them: nevertheless marks that contrast.

gaps.sentence: The plan was expensive; ___, the board approved it.
gaps.explanation: The approval happens in spite of the cost: nevertheless signals concession.

gaps.sentence: He passed the oral exam ___ the fact that he had barely revised.
gaps.explanation: 'The fact that' turns the clause into a noun phrase, which 'despite' requires.

gaps.sentence: ___ the north coast is rocky, the southern beaches are soft golden sand.
gaps.explanation: 'While' can contrast two clauses in a single sentence.

gaps.sentence: The lecture was dull; ___, the students stayed awake out of politeness.
I will send the report today ___ you asked for it early.
